title: GPU occupancy sweeper — continuous-batching sizing notes
content:
Summary:

This working note describes a lightweight "sweeper" model and spreadsheet layout used to explore GPU occupancy / concurrency tradeoffs for continuous-batching inference. Goal is to produce a small, repeatable sweep that ties: (1) continuous-batch window (W), (2) per-GPU concurrency cap (C), and (3) workload arrival/length shape to p95 latency and dollars/token.

Why this is different from prior docs:
- Focus on occupancy as the primary control knob (compute time amortized across wall-time) rather than raw average batch size.
- Sweeper is intentionally conservative: it models kernel overheads, cold-batch penalties, and prefix/KV-cache reuse explicitly so results map well to running clusters.
- Spreadsheet-first (quick sensitivity) plus a small discrete-event sim to validate edges.

Definitions & baseline assumptions (changeable in sheet):
- Arrival model: configurable (Poisson, bursty-CV=2, real traces import). Default: bursty arrival with CV=1.6 and time-varying rate (diurnal spike).
- Request payload:
  - prompt_tokens_mean = 120 (sd 60)
  - gen_tokens_mean = 40 (sd 30)
  - effective_total_tokens = prompt + gen adjusted by prefix_hit_rate
- Prefix/KV cache hit rate (r_cache): fraction of prompt KV cached. Default r_cache=0.55. Cache hits reduce per-request token compute by ~prompt_tokens * 0.85 (empirical).
- Kernel overhead per batch (t_kernel_ms): 1.8 ms (launch + scheduling + memcpy-ish).
- Per-token compute time (t_token_ms) on a reference GPU: 0.12 ms/token (depends on quantization/attention implementation).
- Cold context penalty (p_cold_ms): when a new model instance warms, additional 6-12 ms amortizable per batch in first N batches.
- GPU cost baseline: $3.20 / GPU-hour (on-demand), reserved discount scenarios are modeled as multipliers.

Core equations used in the sheet/sim:
- batch_compute_ms = t_kernel_ms + t_token_ms * total_tokens_in_batch
- occupancy = sum(batch_compute_ms over wall_time_window) / wall_time_window
- per-request generation_time_ms = (assigned_batch_compute_ms * (request_tokens / total_tokens_in_batch)) approximated by proportional split + queue_wait_ms + kernel_overhead_share
- cost_per_request = (batch_compute_ms / 1000 / 3600) * gpu_hourly_rate / batch_request_count

Queueing and scheduling model (simplified used by sweeper):
- Single queue per-GPU (we treat routing and inter-GPU balancing as orthogonal). FIFO batching with continuous-window W: any request that arrives within W of scheduled tick is eligible to join the batch.
- Max batch size: effectively unbounded but constrained by concurrency (C) and GPU memory estimate. We cap at a heuristic B_max = floor(mem_budget / per_token_mem).
- Concurrency C: maximum number of simultaneous batches the GPU will compute. If more batches scheduled, requests queue until a slot frees.
- Continuous batching heuristics implemented: sliding-window commit every T_commit (<= W) to avoid long tail. We default T_commit = W/4 for responsiveness.

Spreadsheet layout (tabs & key columns):
- Tab: sweeper-config (parameters editable): arrival trace selector, W (ms), C, t_token_ms, t_kernel_ms, p_cold_ms, gpu_cost_hr, r_cache, batch_commit_delta
- Tab: synthetic-trace (columns): seq_idx, arrival_ts_ms, prompt_tokens, gen_tokens, prefix_id, kv_hit_boolean
- Tab: sim-results (columns): request_id, assigned_batch_id, assigned_gpu_id, batch_start_ms, batch_end_ms, queue_wait_ms, gen_compute_ms, total_latency_ms, cost_gpu_seconds, notes
- Tab: sweep-summary (columns): W_ms, C, avg_batch_size, occupancy_pct, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, cost_per_1M_tokens, gpu_hours_consumed, reserved_discount_applied

How p95 is computed in this workflow:
- Run the sim over a realistic trace of N requests (>100k) or a synthetic sample that matches percentile shapes.
- Collect total_latency_ms per request (arrival->end of generation).
- p95 = 95th percentile of total_latency_ms. We also compute conditional p95 on large requests (tokens > 250) since they dominate tails.

Practical heuristics & decision rules (for sizing):
1) Pick target_p95 (e.g., 150 ms for low-latency interactive path, 500 ms for background generation).
2) Sweep W across [6 ms, 200 ms] and C across [1, 8] and find minimal cost config satisfying p95 <= target_p95 and occupancy >= min_occupancy (min_occupancy default 18%).
3) Prefer configs where occupancy is in [18%, 55%]. Below ~18% indicates idle GPUs; above ~55% starts having steepening tails and SLO violations.
4) If occupancy too high but p95 ok, consider raising C (if memory allows) rather than increasing W to avoid adding queueing for single-request latency sensitive flows.

Sample synthetic sweep (toy numbers) — keep these as examples only:
- baseline: W=15ms, C=2 -> occupancy 24%, avg_batch=3.1, p95=220ms, cost_per_1M_tokens=$58
- wider-window: W=80ms, C=1 -> occupancy 44%, avg_batch=6.7, p95=360ms, cost_per_1M_tokens=$36
- deeper-concurrency: W=20ms, C=4 -> occupancy 42%, avg_batch=3.9, p95=190ms, cost_per_1M_tokens=$33
Insight: concurrency often gives better tail behavior for the same occupancy because it allows parallel small batches instead of a single giant scheduled batch that inflates queueing for late arrivals.

Checklist for mapping sim -> prod config: (short list)
- Validate t_token_ms and t_kernel_ms against a small microbenchmark run on the target instance and update sheet cells.
- Re-run sweeper with recent 24h arrival trace (anon, sample) for p95 estimates.
- Project cost under three pricing bands: on-demand, 25% reserved, 50% reserved.
- Verify memory headroom for C and worst-case batch. Backstop: auto-failover to smaller model variant if OOM risk detected.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How to fold in model-quantization state transitions (int8 vs int4) which change both t_token_ms and per-token memory linearly — we currently sweep t_token_ms but not memory fragmentation behavior.
- Interaction with prefix-sharding across GPUs: if prefix lookup is remote, additional network latency changes p95 shape nonlinearly. Need microbench to parameterize.
- Real trace CV and diurnal shapes vary by customer — consider storing a small catalog of trace archetypes in the sheet.

Validation plan (small experiments to run on staging cluster):
1) Microbench tick: measure t_kernel_ms and t_token_ms with 10k synthetic requests at low concurrency. Record effective overheads by batch size. Update sheet.
2) Small cluster sweep: pick 3 (W,C) points from the sweeper frontier and run for 6 hours each using replayed production trace (sampling 1/10). Compare measured p95 vs sim p95; iterate on model.
3) Regression harness: add unit tests for the sim that assert monotonicity: increasing W should not reduce occupancy; increasing C should not increase avg_batch_size beyond memory.

Next steps / action items (owners):
- Evelyn: push first version of spreadsheet and sim script to the linked spreadsheet + PR the sim harness. (target: 2026-03-07)
- Samir: run microbench and post t_token_ms and kernel overhead numbers to the sheet. (target: 2026-03-14)
- Priya: prepare 24h trace sample & anonymize, add as trace option. (target: 2026-03-10)
- Miguel: prototype a small chart that shows occupancy vs p95 vs cost (tri-axis) for the sweeper output. (target: 2026-03-09)

Notes-to-self / rough TODOs in sheet:
- Add column for 'percent requests served from cache' vs 'kvs remote miss penalty'.
- Add toggle for staggered commit (commit jitter) to simulate realistic scheduler jitter.
- Expose a per-tenant param so we can sweep mixed-traffic (latency-sensitive + background) mixes.

References & links:
- sim spreadsheet (see linked_artifacts)
- Related tickets: SRV-4100 (continuous batching rollout questions), SLO-125 (interactive p95 target), DEVOPS-88 (reserved pricing modeling)

If you want a shorter extraction: run the "sweeper-config" tab with your target p95 and a recent trace, then run the sim script (sheet has an embedded Apps Script runner) and review sweep-summary. The quick path identifies 3 Pareto candidates (low-latency, low-cost, balanced).

End of note.
